passage: Fossil fuels like coal and petroleum are finite natural resources formed over millions of years from the remains of ancient vegetation and tiny marine organisms buried under high pressure and temperature. Unlike renewable energy, these fuels cannot be recreated in a laboratory or by human technology because the geological conditions required for their formation are no longer present. Petroleum is not stored in large underground lakes; instead, it is trapped in the pores of porous sedimentary rocks, often beneath an impermeable layer of rock. During the refining process, crude oil is separated into various useful components through fractional distillation, which separates substances based on their different boiling points. This process yields not only liquid fuels like petrol and diesel but also solids like paraffin wax and gases like LPG. Coal tar, a thick black liquid obtained during coal processing, is a versatile starting material used in the manufacturing of synthetic dyes, drugs, perfumes, and plastics, in addition to its use in surfacing roads. Because these resources are limited and take millions of years to form, we must use them judiciously to ensure they last for future generations.

items.evidence: Unlike renewable energy, these fuels cannot be recreated in a laboratory or by human technology because the geological conditions required for their formation are no longer present.
items.q: Why can scientists not make new coal in a laboratory today?
options: The Earth conditions that formed it are gone
It came from dinosaur bones, which are rare now
New coal forms daily, so there is no need
It is renewable, so making it is pointless
items.explain: Coal cannot be made by people because the Earth conditions needed to form it no longer exist.

wrong.why: thinks coal comes from dinosaur remains
thinks fossil fuels form every day
mixes up fossil fuels with renewable energy

items.evidence: Petroleum is not stored in large underground lakes; instead, it is trapped in the pores of porous sedimentary rocks, often beneath an impermeable layer of rock.
items.q: A company drills deep to find crude oil. Where will the oil most likely be?
options: In tiny holes inside sedimentary rock
In a large lake deep underground
In open space above the impermeable rock
In layers of buried dinosaur remains
items.explain: Petroleum is trapped in the pores of sedimentary rock, usually under an impermeable layer, not in underground lakes.

wrong.why: thinks petroleum sits in underground lakes or caves
reverses the position of the rock layers
thinks fossil fuels come from dinosaurs

items.evidence: This process yields not only liquid fuels like petrol and diesel but also solids like paraffin wax and gases like LPG.
items.q: Ritu thinks everything made from refining crude oil is runny like petrol. Which product proves her wrong?
options: Paraffin wax, which is a solid
Diesel, which is a thick fuel
Coal tar, which is a black liquid
items.explain: Refining gives solids like paraffin wax too, so not every petroleum product is a liquid.

wrong.why: thinks all petroleum products are liquids
thinks wax only comes from bees or plants
picks a nearby product that comes from coal, not petroleum

items.evidence: Coal tar, a thick black liquid obtained during coal processing, is a versatile starting material used in the manufacturing of synthetic dyes, drugs, perfumes, and plastics, in addition to its use in surfacing roads.
items.q: Meena says coal tar is good for nothing but making roads. What does the lesson say?
options: It also goes into dyes, medicines and plastics
It is used only to cover road surfaces
It is filtered to make petrol and diesel
It is a solid wax used for candles
items.explain: Coal tar is used to make dyes, drugs, perfumes and plastics, as well as to surface roads.

wrong.why: thinks coal tar is only for roads
thinks refining is filtering, and mixes coal tar with petroleum
mixes up coal tar with paraffin wax
